method: Run each case with the skill and without it (same model, same prompt), 3 runs each. The fixture's conventions deliberately differ from the skill's defaults: passing means the project won.

evals.prompt: Add a QuantityStepper component (minus / count / plus) with a test.
expectations: Reads AGENTS.md (or runs scripts/conventions.py) before writing code and says which convention sources it used
Creates src/components/quantity-stepper/index.tsx and styles.ts (kebab-case folder + index, styles next to it)
Arrow-function component with a default export and `interface QuantityStepperProps`
Styles with styled-components only: no inline style, no CSS file, no Tailwind
Test at src/components/__tests__/quantity-stepper.test.tsx using Testing Library role queries and user-event with Vitest
Uses <button type="button"> with accessible names for minus/plus

evals.prompt:
Review this component: function Total({ items }) { const [total, setTotal] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { setTotal(items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price, 0)) }, [items]); return

{total}

}
expectations: Flags the effect as derived state and replaces it with a value computed during render
Does not recommend useMemo as the primary fix unless it justifies the cost

evals.prompt: The cart count should also show in the header. Wire it up.
expectations: Uses the existing zustand store (useCartStore) instead of creating a React Context or prop drilling
Does not add a new state library
Does not flag the default export, arrow function or interface props: they are the project's conventions
Reports no high or medium findings and does not invent problems
